In Amazon's Finance Technology group, we build the detection systems (machine learning, and increasingly agentic AI) that defend Amazon against theft, fraud, abuse, and waste across the supply chain, retail catalog, and corporate procurement. We turn terabytes of transaction, vendor, and operational data into real-time risk decisions: scoring payments as they happen, surfacing anomalous behavior, and uncovering collusion networks that span thousands of entities.
We're now building the next generation of that platform around generative and agentic AI: multi-agent systems that discover fraud patterns directly from the raw data flowing through Amazon's businesses, working alongside domain experts to turn what they find into production detection logic. The result is a platform where new detection coverage comes not only from engineers, but from agents and the experts who know the fraud best, shipping in days instead of sprints.
You'll build the agent tools, ML pipelines, services, and data infrastructure behind all of this, working with generative AI, large language models, and agent frameworks alongside the anomaly-detection, classification, and graph-modeling techniques they build on. You'll partner directly with applied scientists, fellow engineers, and finance operations teams, and you'll see your ideas reach production in weeks.

Design and build ML pipelines that process terabytes of data and score billions of dollars in transactions.

Build the platform and tooling (governed data access, model deployment, and self-service rule authoring) that lets agents and non-engineers ship detection logic safely and fast.
Take models and agents from prototype to reliable, real-time production systems, and work directly with internal customers to turn feedback into shipped improvements.
A day in the life
You'll partner with applied scientists, software engineers, and finance operations teams across Amazon. Disha is a step toward that future. Disha is an AI health coach that supports people through personalized, ongoing conversations across chat and voice. jobs.description:
About the role 
 Recruitcha.ai is sales intelligence for recruitment agencies. We watch the market for hiring signals so agency recruiters know which companies to call, who to talk to, and why now. Our products include Jobs Listener, Social Listener, ATS Graveyard and Market Mapping.
 We're three people. We're bootstrapped and profitable, with 100+ agencies using our platform. The founders spent 10+ years running and selling into recruiting agencies, so we already know what our customers need. Our job is to build it well.
 We built the first version fast, using AI heavily. It works, and customers pay for it. Some of it is held together with duct tape. We're hiring our first engineer to turn it into a platform that scales without losing the speed that got us here.
At a glance Location : Remote, with 2+ hours of daily overlap with US PST time
 Team : 3 people today; you'd be the first engineer
 Reports to: The founders
What you'll own You'll decide what to refactor, what to rebuild, and what to leave alone. Here are the problems on the table today:
 Signal ingestion. We pull hiring signals from job boards, ATS pages, social activity and third-party data providers. Much of it runs on scheduled jobs that fail silently. It needs to become a reliable pipeline with monitoring, retries and deduplication.
 Data model at scale. Companies, contacts, jobs and signals have grown faster than our Supabase schema was designed for. Queries are slowing down and the data has duplicates.
 Agentic workflows. Our AI agents research accounts, find decision-makers and draft outreach. They work well in demos. Before we can trust them across every customer, they need evals, guardrails, cost controls and observability.
 Engineering foundations. We need CI, tests where they matter, staging environments, and a deploy process that doesn't depend on luck.
 New product. Customers ask for features every week. You'll work with the founders to decide what to build and then ship it across the full stack.
 Your first 90 days By day 30: You've shipped to production, sat in on customer calls, and mapped the codebase. You've told us what's fragile and what's fine.
 By day 60: You've fixed the worst reliability problem, likely signal ingestion. Failures now alert someone instead of disappearing.
 By day 90: You own deploys, monitoring and the technical roadmap. You're shipping customer features every week, and we make architecture decisions based on your judgment.
 Our stack Frontend: Next.js, TypeScript
 Backend: Node.js, Python, Supabase (Postgres)
 AI: model providers, e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google
 You don't need experience with all of these. We want a strong engineer first, and the stack can change if you make the case.

HWA International builds the trust accounting software that bank trust departments, credit unions,  
foundations, and family offices run their fiduciary operations on. We are an AI-first engineering  
organization, and agentic coding tools are how we build. Our platform is in a significant modernization,  
and this role is one of the engineers who builds it.  
Agentic tooling lets us understand existing behavior and specify what comes next far faster than that  
work could be done by hand. You will use it to do exactly that, then build the modern platform end to  
end: the C# and .NET services, the web front end, and the AWS infrastructure they run on. This is a full-  
stack role, and you own the infrastructure your work runs on.  
Accounting accuracy is the product, so correctness is the bar. Anything new has to produce the same  
results as what it replaces, or better, and proving that is part of the job.  
You will work within an architecture set by engineering leadership, with real influence on it. We work to  
modern engineering standards: trunk-based development on GitHub, continuous integration,  
infrastructure as code, and feature flags.

and the web front end that sits on them, against the architecture and patterns the team has set.  

* Own the infrastructure for what you deliver. Within the cloud architecture engineering

leadership sets, define and maintain your AWS environments as code, along with the  
networking, managed databases, and services behind them, so every environment is  
reproducible and version controlled.  

* Own delivery and observability. Build and run the CI/CD pipelines, staged rollout, and feature

flags that take your work to production, and the monitoring, logging, and alerting that tell us  
how it behaves there.  

* Work out what existing code does and write it down. Use agentic tooling to analyze established

application and database logic, then produce a clear written specification of the behavior that  
has to be preserved.  

* Move business logic into application code and prove it matches. Relocate rules wherever they

live today, including inside the database, into maintainable, tested application code. Build the  
data migration paths and test harnesses that show the modern platform's calculations match  
the existing ones.

* Verify what the tools give you. Agentic tooling drafts the analysis, the documentation, and

much of the code. An agent's account of what existing code does is a hypothesis until you have  
read the code and confirmed it. Characterization tests come before behavior changes.  

* Own the work in production. Whatever ships under your name is yours, from the first analysis

through to how it behaves in production. Take part in incident response, communicate clearly  
while an issue is open, and follow through to root cause and a durable fix.
